run.change_description:
ec0e33b3 Avoid setting a connection's `ca_certs` or `ca_cert_dir` attributes when `verify=True`

8f954567 Use a default SSLContext with the default CA bundle loaded when `verify=True`

f21e70bf Rename default SSLContext to make it private by convention

4089f3dc Wrap line to comply with CI lint

summary.intent: Cache one SSLContext with the default CA bundle preloaded and reuse it for every default-verified (`verify=True`) HTTPS connection, so urllib3 no longer reruns the slow `SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations()` on every request; `verify=False` and explicit CA-path behavior are meant to stay as before (user-supplied PR body for psf/requests#6667, no linked issue).
summary.issue_fit: No linked issue; alignment judged against the PR body's own stated goal and its 'verify=True/False still behave as expected' claim.
summary.coverage: Full merge-base diff reviewed (src/requests/adapters.py, the only changed file, one complete chunk). Reused connection-pool caching in the same file (_get_connection, cert_verify) read in full for interaction with the new module-level context.
check_details: Reviewer-executed: PYTHONPATH=<clone>/src pytest tests/test_requests.py tests/test_adapters.py at head 4089f3dc65f783beaa53cc032958ab625440d0ac — 23 failed, 305 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xpassed. Same command re-run against an unpacked copy of the merge-base's src tree (8dd3b26b) reproduces the identical 23 failures verbatim, so all are pre-existing/environmental (no-network httpbin fixtures, plus three TLS fixtures failing on 'Missing Authority Key Identifier' from this machine's OpenSSL rejecting the bundled test certs), not introduced by this diff.

Reviewer-executed custom probe (scratch script, not added to the clone): monkeypatches certifi.where() to a test CA before importing requests, counts ssl.SSLContext.load_verify_locations calls, and drives three verify=True requests against a local TLSServer. Call count is exactly 1 (the module-level preload) after import and stays there through pool creation, confirming the per-request reload is actually skipped; the requests themselves fail on the same pre-existing AKI fixture issue, not on this change.

Reviewer-executed: reproduced with a two-line repro (patch certifi.where() to a nonexistent path, then `import requests`) that `import requests` raises unhandled FileNotFoundError at head but succeeds at merge-base with the same broken bundle path, isolating the new must-fix finding to this diff.

findings.title: Defer the CA-bundle preload instead of running it at import
findings.trigger: `import requests` now unconditionally runs `_preloaded_ssl_context.load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))` at module load, before any request is made or any `verify` value is known.
findings.impact: If the default CA bundle (`certifi.where()`) is missing, stripped, or unreadable, the bare import now raises an unhandled `FileNotFoundError` and crashes the whole process — even programs that only ever pass `verify=False` or an explicit CA path and never touch the default bundle. Reproduced directly: with a broken bundle path, `import requests` succeeds at the merge-base (the check was lazy, inside `cert_verify()`, only for a default-bundle verified request, and raised a clear `requests`-style `OSError`) but fails at head.
findings.change: Move the `create_urllib3_context()`/`load_verify_locations()` pair behind a function invoked only from the `verify is True` branch of `_urllib3_request_context` (e.g. cache it with `functools.lru_cache`), so the load stays lazy and any failure still reaches only default-bundle-verified callers with the previous clear error.

observations.fact: urllib3 2.8.0's `_ssl_wrap_socket_and_match_hostname` runs `context.verify_mode = resolve_cert_reqs(cert_reqs)` on every connect, including for the shared `_preloaded_ssl_context`; this looked like the reconfiguration hazard tiran warned about in review, but it always writes the same `CERT_REQUIRED` value back (the shared context is only ever used on the `verify=True` path), so it is a redundant write, not an observed defect.
observations.evidence: urllib3/connection.py:1040-1042 (installed 2.8.0); src/requests/adapters.py:91-99 only reaches the `_preloaded_ssl_context` branch when `verify is True`, which always pairs with `cert_reqs="CERT_REQUIRED"`.

requirements.evidence: adapters.py:75-98 builds one cached SSLContext with the CA bundle preloaded and passes it as pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] for verify=True, leaving ca_certs/ca_cert_dir/ca_cert_data unset; urllib3's ssl_wrap_socket (util/ssl_.py:413) only calls load_verify_locations when one of those is truthy, so it is skipped on every connect. Confirmed dynamically: a probe against the installed urllib3 2.8.0 shows load_verify_locations called exactly once (at import), not once per request, across three verify=True connections.

requirements.source: spec-requests-pr-6667/pr-body/"You can test against https://invalid.badssl.com to check that verify=True and verify=False still behave as expected"
requirements.evidence: cert_reqs stays CERT_REQUIRED for verify=True and CERT_NONE for verify=False (adapters.py:91-99), and verify=True still enforces hostname/cert validation via the same preloaded context's default check_hostname. Live cross-check against invalid.badssl.com is unavailable (no network, per run policy); local TLS fixtures that would exercise this fail identically at merge-base and head from a pre-existing OpenSSL 'Missing Authority Key Identifier' fixture mismatch unrelated to this change, so behavior parity rests on this code trace rather than an end-to-end pass.
